changelog: Rewrote [When to Segment] rule 4 to explicitly forbid boundaries inside incomplete coordinate structures (X and Y, X or Y) until ALL coordinates and the closing conjunction have arrived.

Added new [When to Segment] rule 4a: 'After a prepositional phrase object arrives, if the phrase completes a noun phrase.' This permits boundaries after full NP closes, preventing early cuts before preposition objects.
Added new [When to Segment] rule 4b: 'After a negation, reversal, or exclusive marker (not, only, without, rejected, etc.) that settles polarity or scope of the preceding claim.'

Rewrote [Never Segment] rule 6 to forbid boundaries: (a) inside coordinate structures before the final coordinate arrives; (b) after a noun heading a prepositional phrase, before the preposition's object; (c) before negations, exclusive markers, or scope-limiting modifiers that reverse or restrict the preceding assertion.
Added [Never Segment] rule 7: 'Before a relative clause or causal modifier that immediately follows a noun phrase, if the modifier is not yet complete.'
Added [Never Segment] rule 8: 'After a passive voice verb, before the agent phrase (by-phrase) arrives, unless the agent is absent from the source.'

Rewrote [Priority Rules] to demote boundaries at relative position 0/3 (early in sentence) and after commas that precede incomplete coordinate structures or polarity reversals to lowest confidence (rank 11–12).
Ranked boundaries after COMPLETE coordinate structures and after polarity-settled clauses (negation/reversal/exclusive marker fully visible) as highest confidence (rank 1–2).
Added [Examples — Segment] showing safe cuts after complete coordinates, after negations, and after prepositional phrase objects.
Added [Examples — Do NOT Segment] showing unsafe cuts inside coordinates, before negations, and before preposition objects.
